title: Students plan End Rape Culture protest on NDSU campus in Fargo

tea.why: Students are protesting against campus rape culture and expressing frustration regarding how sexual assault allegations are handled.
tea.want: Organizers call for an end to campus rape culture and seek to support sexual assault survivors.
tea.changed: Oct 23: Organizers announced a campus protest scheduled for November 1 at Churchill Field.

summary: Students at North Dakota State University plan to hold an End Rape Culture protest and solidarity demonstration on Churchill Field in Fargo. Hosted by the Women’s Activist Organization, the event invites students from NDSU, Concordia College, and Minnesota State University Moorhead, along with local community members. According to the group's president, the demonstration was inspired by a civil lawsuit and reopened criminal case involving sexual assault allegations at Cornell University, as well as local frustrations with campus climate regarding sexual violence and how women who speak out are treated. Organizers have scheduled sign-making sessions ahead of the rally. No official university response was reported regarding the protest itself.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Women's Activist Organization announced an End Rape Culture protest scheduled for November 1 at Churchill Field.
